intentAndPurpose.intent: Chunky 160×32 fingertip-friendly slider. The track is the tap target; the fill represents the value. Ideal for touch devices, TV remotes, and large-target contexts.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial uncontrolled value. Defaults to `50` (Figma); pass `0` explicitly to retain the pre-conformance default.

props.name: progressStyle
props.description: Canonical public name for Figma's `trackStyle` axis.

props.name: start
props.description: Decorative, non-interactive OneUI Icon rendered in the leading cap. The complete slider owns the accessible name; do not pass IconButton.

props.name: trackStyle
props.description: Deprecated alias matching the actual Figma component-set property. `progressStyle` wins when both are supplied.

props.name: value
props.description: Canonical TouchSlider values are scalar. Arrays remain accepted as a deprecated compatibility shape and preserve their array callback shape; use Slider `type="range"` for a supported multi-thumb control.

interactionBehavior.summary: TouchSlider is a chunky single-thumb fill control: there is no visible knob. The whole 32px pill is the hit target (with a 44px slop via a pseudo-element), a tap anywhere on the track moves the fill to that point — the value jumps but the fill eases across via a real `width`/`height` transition rather than snapping — and a drag captures the pointer on the Control. The thumb is a zero-size, `pointer-events: none` host for the hidden range input. Keyboard uses the same macOS-style accelerator as Slider.
press: Pointer-down anywhere on the Control — including the hit-slop `::before` that extends the 32px pill to 44px — is a track press: Base UI jumps the (invisible) thumb to that point and then `setPointerCapture`s for the drag.
There is no separate thumb to grab; `pointer-events: none` on `.thumb` makes every press hit the track.
The start-slot icon is `inert` and `pointer-events: none`, so a tap on the leading cap still drags the fill rather than activating the icon.
focus: Keyboard focus draws the two-layer halo on the CONTROL (the pill), not on a knob: `--Stroke-XL` gap in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer `--Informative-Bold` ring (always Informative, regardless of appearance).
The selector is `:has(:focus-visible)`, not `:focus-within`, so a mouse click that focuses the hidden input does not paint the halo.
keyboard: The same capture-phase accelerator as Slider intercepts `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` (horizontal) or `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` (vertical), `PageUp` / `PageDown`, and `Shift+Arrow`. Repeats accelerate (×2 / ×5 / `largeStep`); `Shift` and page keys always use `largeStep`.
`Home` / `End` fall through to Base UI and jump to `min` / `max`.

On a horizontal TouchSlider, `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` are not accelerated; they fall through and Base UI steps them by Root's `step` (TouchSlider always passes the public `step`, unlike Slider's `dragStep`). Same for `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` when vertical.
`readOnly` sets `aria-readonly`, keeps the input focusable (not natively disabled), and both cancels Base UI changes and skips the accelerator. `disabled` natively disables the input.
disabled: `disabled` dims the root to `--Disabled-Opacity` and sets `cursor: not-allowed`. The Control, its hit-slop `::before`, the thumb, and the input all get `pointer-events: none`.
The not-allowed cursor is on the root, so it is observable — this is not the Button-style cursor gap.

`readOnly` is stricter than Slider's: the whole root gets `pointer-events: none` (cursor `default` on the Control), so pointer dragging is blocked, while the input stays focusable for AT. It does not dim.
touch: The visual pill is `--Spacing-8` (32px) thick; `.control::before` extends the hit area by `--TouchSlider-hitSlop` (`--Spacing-Negative-1-5`) so the target is 44px without changing layout. Because the slop belongs to Base UI's Control, presses in that extra band still jump-and-drag.
Root and Control set `touch-action: none` so a drag does not scroll the page.

There is no hover fill or knob growth — a tap's only visual is the fill easing into place: `.indicator` transitions its `width` / `height` over `--Motion-Duration-M` with `--Motion-Easing-Entrance-Moderate`, so it glides to the new point rather than snapping there. `prefers-reduced-motion` keeps only the colour fade and drops the size animation.
